answer: Umber-beacon echo-closure: each agent periodically emits a beacon with a random umber nonce; peers forward it and return echo paths. Relay admission requires k disjoint echo paths whose latency/jitter fingerprints match independent network regions. Sybils on one host or NAT produce correlated echoes; isolated nodes cannot synthesize diverse paths. Attacker cost: operating many real, well-connected relay endpoints and sustaining distinct path latency/jitter, not just IDs.
